data.narrative:
Matter is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Adi Prasad, Charly Mwangi, Aish Varadhan, and Aditya Ranjan, having raised $21M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private robotics firms (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI) and one public comparable.

Given Matter's early stage and limited granular peer data, the stage-progression method provides the primary valuation anchor. Using $14M as a proxy for total raised and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for Seed-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $35M. This multiplier reflects observed progression patterns within the Robotics & Manufacturing sector, though the narrow peer set at identical stage precluded robust median-based triangulation—insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables met quality thresholds to support a peer-median approach independently.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $30M to $40M, with a median of $35M. Key uncertainties include the lack of sufficiently granular peer comparables at Matter's specific stage and the inherent variability in early-stage step-up multiples across robotics sub-verticals. Any refinement of this range would benefit from additional data on capital efficiency, customer traction, or technical differentiation relative to the identified peer set.
